source.title: Reasoning Bias of Next Token Prediction Training
source.authors: Peng-Xiao Lin; Zhongwang Zhang; Z. Xu

record.file_problem: Text includes the full paper and appendix. Some figure labels and plot values are garbled; no precise values were reconstructed from figures.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares test performance after two training objectives on reasoning and classification datasets. It does not test the claim versions’ specific interventions or measurements, such as random-label memorization, width, optimizer choice, or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: The study tests next-token prediction (NTP) against critical-token prediction (CTP), not the listed versions’ conditions. PrOntoQA and several other tasks are synthetic; the paper also reports natural-language benchmark results. Figure-only comparisons without a recoverable value or explicit textual outcome are not rows. OOV and compositional results are excluded because the prompt treats those as separate.
record.test_reason: The study compares next-token prediction with critical-token prediction in transformers. Its results concern training objectives, reasoning, transfer and robustness, without testing any of V1–V8. Its weight-normalized perturbation experiment does not measure V7's generalization gaps or compare generalization-measure rankings within a convolutional family.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors attribute NTP's reasoning and robustness advantages during training from scratch to noise-induced regularization, and favor CTP for supervised finetuning because it learns faster with little additional benefit from NTP. Their findings also include early transfer benefits with greater catastrophic forgetting, mixed classification results, and task-dependent flatness differences.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares NTP with CTP on GPT-2 reasoning and classification tasks. It does not use the original interventions or measurements described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported NTP advantage varies by task category: it is described as stronger on reasoning tasks and diminished or mixed on text classification. The paper also reports different outcomes between training from scratch and finetuning pretrained GPT-2.

fits_no_version.finding: On original PrOntoQA, NTP reaches 100% test accuracy versus approximately 80% for CTP. On RobustLR, NTP learns some logical patterns while CTP remains at chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested transformers trained from scratch, NTP can improve reasoning-task accuracy over CTP, with task-dependent benefits.

fits_no_version.finding: On 1-hop OOV PrOntoQA, NTP achieves nearly 100% accuracy versus approximately 70% for CTP; both methods struggle with the 2-hop OOV task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NTP's advantage over CTP on vocabulary generalization depends on reasoning depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.3 scales random weight perturbations by each model's overall parameter norm. NTP is substantially flatter on the anchor task, while differences are more nuanced on other tasks and the authors identify an output-space confound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relationship between training objective and transformer loss-landscape flatness depends on the task and the loss being compared.

fits_no_version.finding: With 1,000 or 2,000 poisoned addition examples, NTP has higher peak test accuracy and later degradation, while CTP memorizes the poisoned labels faster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NTP can delay fitting sparse erroneous labels and improve interim clean-test performance relative to CTP.

record.problems: The paper reports exact textual outcomes for only some comparisons; many cross-task and robustness results are presented in plots without recoverable values. The study does not test random-label memorization or the listed claim versions’ named conditions. Some datasets are synthetic, and its stated three-run standard deviation applies to the anchor-function depth experiment, not the extracted test-accuracy rows.
record.rows_left_out: OOV PrOntoQA rows R3–R4 are retained as study results but are outside the claim’s in-distribution scope. Compositional anchor-function results and additional OOV results are omitted from rows because the prompt separates these behaviors from the claim. Figure-only comparisons without a textual outcome or reliably assignable values were omitted, including many dataset-specific comparisons in Figure 4 and robustness plots.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training, random-label fitting capacity, and chance-level held-out performance under random labels. Sparse poisoned addition labels do not supply this comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation or weight decay. Disabling dropout in the recipe supplies no dropout comparison.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, including rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. Generalization in the broad sense is insufficient to link these experiments to V1–V8. The additional findings listed under fits_no_version do not constitute missing results for a tested version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweep beyond interpolation on the specified image datasets.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adjustments.
Dropout effects and its interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps across the specified convolutional networks.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
